Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to arrive in Ankara today, the first bilateral visit to Türkiye by a Canadian leader, as he seeks to reduce Canada’s reliance on the United States. 
He is set to meet President Erdogan and sign a declaration deepening cooperation in areas including defense and energy.
A Turkish diplomatic source said ties will be upgraded to a “strategic partnership.” 
Carney is on a global trade push to shield Canada from Trump’s tariffs. 
He aims to double Canada’s non-U.S. exports within a decade. 
The two leaders launched free-trade talks at the NATO summit in Ankara in July. 
Türkiye is looking for investment in its defense industry, nuclear power plants and mining sector. 
Source: Reuters
